events.title: The death of Pope St. Martin I in exile
events.shortBlurb: Martin I, who would not bend to the emperor's Typos, died an exile at Cherson, the last pope the Church reckons a martyr…
body: Martin I, a Tuscan of Todi, had served as apocrisiarius at Constantinople before the clergy and people of Rome made him pope in July 649 — without waiting, in defiance of custom, for the emperor's mandate. That October he gathered one hundred and five bishops in the Lateran, and in twenty canons they condemned the Monothelite doctrine and the Typos of the Emperor Constans II.

The emperor's answer came slowly but surely. In June 653 the exarch's men arrested the pope in the Lateran basilica itself and shipped him to Constantinople, where a tribunal condemned him for treason; he was stripped of his pallium, flogged in public, and banished to Cherson in the Crimea.

There, on 16 September 655, he died of want and of his wounds, his letters from exile breathing still a dry irony over the price of bread. East and West together venerate him as the last martyr-pope; the doctrine for which he suffered, two wills in the one Christ, was defined at the Sixth Ecumenical Council a generation later, and his companion in confession, St. Maximus, bore the same witness with his own maimed body.
